obligations.note: The change does not modify rbac.py or access-policy.json for payments; the access matrix is unchanged and the control test passed.
The auditor role and its grants in the access policy are untouched; the new route requires manage_payees which the auditor does not hold.
The segregation-of-duties entries in access-policy.json and rbac.py are unchanged; it_admin still cannot approve or release payments.

The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses action manage_payees, which is listed as privileged in controls/payments/access-policy.json, yet is declared with mfa=False. The CI control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa explicitly fails on this route.
No session or policy-parameter code is touched; the 15-minute privileged idle limit remains intact.
The new reopen_payee SQL updates only status and closed_at; no NPI columns (account_number, routing_number, tax_id, date_of_birth) are read or written in plaintext.
integrations.py and transports.py are not modified; all outbound endpoints remain on https.
The new service method logs only the action name and payee ID via the audit helper; no NPI value is passed to any log call.
reopen_payee in service.py calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target, and time as required.
audit.py and its retention parameters are untouched; the hash-chained, 7-year retention evidence in the ledger remains valid.
The change adds reopen_payee to store.py but does not modify purge_payee_npi or closed_payees_before; the retention logic is unchanged.
integrations.py and asset-inventory.json are not modified; no new outbound integration is introduced.
The new SQL in store.py ('UPDATE payees SET status = ?... WHERE id = ?') binds payee_id as a parameter; no statement text is built from data.
payments.py (approve, is_fully_approved) is not modified; maker-checker logic is unchanged.
payments.py, policy.py, and policy-params.json are untouched; the dual-control threshold and approver count are unchanged.
payments.py#release and store.py#find_release/add_release are not modified; release idempotency logic is unchanged.
Ticket CHG-24738 is approved by change_manager grace.kim; its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover every changed file.
Mara Costa (mara.costa@fernbrook.example) holds the change_approver role for payments and is not the author (Linh Nguyen); her code_review approval is valid.
There is a single commit (c8cfd68); both the code_review and security_review approvals name that exact commit, so no later commit voids them.
The CI run on the final commit reports 1 failure: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa. The full suite is not passing, violating the requirement that testing on the final commit must be green.

Security-sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store) are touched; Ines Halvorsen (platform-security, security_reviewer) approved with kind security_review on the same commit, and she is not the author.
MFA-1 is violated by the new route, but no approved, unexpired exception in the register covers payments.routes or this component; EXC-0172 is withdrawn and scoped to mortgage.routes only.
ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence) covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py, which this change modifies; the evidence lapses and no new valid evidence (the CI control test fails) replaces it.

summary: The change introduces a POST /payees/{id}/reopen route that uses the privileged action manage_payees but is declared with mfa=False, directly violating MFA-1 and causing the exhaustive control test to fail in CI. Because the CI suite does not pass on the final commit, CHG-4 is also violated. The MFA-1 evidence in the acceptance ledger (ACR-0404) lapses under LAP-1 because routes.py is modified, and no valid exception in the register covers the deviation, failing EXC-1. With four obligations refuted (MFA-1, CHG-4, EXC-1, LAP-1), the change must be rejected; the route must be given mfa=True (or the action reclassified) before resubmission.
